policy: Short practical original-language copy, not extracted Weiser paragraphs.
Independently verified facts scoped to sources, not universal Roman rites.
Calendar, Saints, Pray, Customs Atlas and Special Days retain existing ownership.
Historical indulgences, magical folklore, modern legal obligations and unknown 1962 formulae held separately.

cards.title_en: Ember Days: gratitude, vocations and charity
cards.title_fr: Les Quatre-Temps : action de grâce, vocations et charité
cards.occasion: Four sets of seasonal Ember days in the 1962 calendar
cards.geographic_scope: Historical Latin Catholic practice; obligation depends on actual governing law
cards.description_en: Traditional Ember Days set aside seasonal days of penitence and prayer. Their intentions have included thanksgiving for the fruits of the earth, support for priests and vocations, and charitable help for neighbours.
cards.description_fr: Dans l'usage traditionnel des Quatre-Temps, des journées de pénitence et de prière ponctuent les saisons. Elles sont associées à l'action de grâce pour les récoltes, aux intentions pour les prêtres et les vocations et au secours des personnes démunies.
cards.meaning_en: Ordinary work, harvest and the service of priests are placed before God in a spirit of repentance and gratitude.
cards.meaning_fr: Le travail, les fruits de la terre et le ministère des prêtres sont confiés à Dieu dans un esprit de pénitence et de reconnaissance.
cards.suggested_observance_en: On an Ember day, pray for priests and vocations, thank God for daily bread and make a voluntary act of charity.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Un jour des Quatre-Temps, prier pour les prêtres et les vocations, rendre grâce pour le pain quotidien et accomplir librement un acte de charité.

independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: The source specifically identifies seasonal Ember prayer, fasting, almsgiving, thanksgiving for crops, and petitions for clergy. These are historical 1962-linked meanings, not a current globally binding fast.

cards.publication_caution: Keep the 1962 dates in Calendar, without inventing present fasting obligations or duplicating existing Ember-day prayers.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_fr: Une marche de prière familiale aux Rogations
cards.occasion: Major and Minor Rogation days, where traditionally observed
cards.geographic_scope: Historical Catholic household suggestion; farm, garden or city context
cards.existing_owner: Customs Atlas / Calendar; distinct from parish priestly procession
cards.description_en: A Catholic family guide describes going on a simple prayer walk during the Rogations, asking God's blessing on gardens, crops and the labour of those who provide food. This private act is distinct from the priest-led litanies or blessings.
cards.description_fr: Un ancien guide familial catholique propose une promenade de prière aux Rogations pour confier à Dieu les jardins, les récoltes et le travail de ceux qui produisent la nourriture. Ce geste privé est distinct des litanies et des bénédictions sacerdotales.
cards.meaning_en: Prayer for the harvest recognises dependence on God's providence and the dignity of human labour.
cards.meaning_fr: La prière pour les récoltes rappelle la dépendance envers la Providence et la dignité du travail humain.
cards.suggested_observance_en: Take a short family walk, or pause beside a garden, to pray for farmers and give thanks for creation; attend a real parish Rogation if offered.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Faire une courte marche en famille, ou s'arrêter dans un jardin, pour prier pour les agriculteurs et remercier Dieu de la création ; participer aux Rogations paroissiales là où elles existent.

independent_witnesses.issuer: Mary Reed Newland via Catholic Culture, family liturgical custom
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: An independent Catholic family custom guide explicitly proposes a family walk asking for God's blessing on gardens and fields. A family prayer is distinct from a priest's processional blessing.

cards.publication_caution: Do not copy ministerial blessing formulas into family instructions or imply a modern universal obligation.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: Shrove Tuesday and the traditional pancake
cards.title_fr: Le Mardi gras et les crêpes de la veille du Carême
cards.geographic_scope: British and Irish household tradition, with related customs elsewhere
cards.description_en: In parts of England and Ireland, families made pancakes on Shrove Tuesday before Lent, traditionally using eggs, milk and fat that older fasting disciplines restricted. The familiar meal marked a change from festive preparation to penitential observance.
cards.description_fr: En Angleterre et en Irlande, des familles préparaient des crêpes le Mardi gras, avant le Carême, pour utiliser les œufs, le lait et les matières grasses autrefois restreints par la discipline du jeûne. Ce repas marquait le passage de la fête à la pénitence.
cards.meaning_en: A modest family meal can mark the transition toward Lenten conversion without making pleasure itself an end.
cards.meaning_fr: Un repas familial simple peut marquer la transition vers la conversion du Carême sans faire du plaisir une fin en soi.
cards.suggested_observance_en: If this custom is part of your heritage, prepare pancakes, then discuss a suitable programme of prayer and penance for Lent.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Si cette coutume fait partie de votre tradition familiale, préparer des crêpes puis choisir des engagements adaptés de prière et de pénitence pour le Carême.

weiser_sources.source_title: Shrove Tuesday pancakes and pre-Lenten food usage

independent_witnesses.issuer: Archdiocese of St Louis excerpt on Catholic Culture
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Pancakes prepared in England/Ireland to use eggs, milk and fat before older penitential food restrictions; not a present legal Lenten requirement.

cards.publication_caution: Historical dairy restrictions are not asserted as present universal Catholic law; do not duplicate Confession-module content.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: Adoration along the Corpus Christi procession
cards.title_fr: L'adoration pendant la procession de la Fête-Dieu
cards.occasion: Corpus Christi, only where a Eucharistic procession actually occurs
cards.geographic_scope: Catholic public devotion with local route and ceremonial variations
cards.existing_owner: Existing Corpus Christi Special Days; Customs Atlas context
cards.description_en: Corpus Christi processions bring the Blessed Sacrament through streets and neighbourhoods. The faithful respond with prayer and adoration, sometimes kneeling; local routes may include decorated stations, and a Eucharistic blessing ordinarily concludes the procession.
cards.description_fr: Lors des processions de la Fête-Dieu, le Saint-Sacrement traverse les rues et les quartiers. Les fidèles manifestent leur adoration par la prière et parfois l'agenouillement ; des reposoirs peuvent jalonner le parcours, qui se termine normalement par la bénédiction eucharistique.
cards.meaning_en: The procession gives public witness to belief in Christ's Real Presence in the Eucharist.
cards.meaning_fr: La procession témoigne publiquement de la foi en la présence réelle du Christ dans l'Eucharistie.
cards.suggested_observance_en: Join your parish's announced procession with reverence; follow its directions for posture and stops rather than assuming a universal route.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Participer avec révérence à une procession effectivement annoncée par sa paroisse ; suivre les indications locales pour les attitudes et les arrêts.

weiser_sources.source_title: Kneeling to adore Eucharist before home on processional route
Corpus Christi stations with prayers and Eucharistic Benediction

independent_witnesses.issuer: Benedict XVI, Corpus Christi homily 22 May 2008
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Public kneeling/adoration accompanying procession confirmed; particular action 'outside one's own home' is not individually verified and must not be asserted.

independent_witnesses.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety and the Liturgy, nos. 162–163
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: The directory acknowledges stops at decorated altars on Eucharistic procession routes and solemn benediction at the conclusion; number/form of stations varies locally and is not 1962 rubric-certified by this witness.

cards.publication_caution: Kneeling in front of a particular private home and a precise number of stops are not independently proved; do not inject new events into the 48-card Mass reader.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: Polish dożynki: the blessed harvest wreath
cards.title_fr: Les dożynki polonaises : couronnes et pains des récoltes
cards.occasion: Late-summer or autumn harvest thanksgiving, as locally scheduled
cards.existing_owner: Customs Atlas / regional history; Calendar contextual link only
cards.description_en: Polish Catholic harvest celebrations, called dożynki, bring the work of farmers before God in thanksgiving. In a documented diocesan observance, a bishop blessed ceremonial harvest wreaths and loaves of bread offered by regional communities.
cards.description_fr: Les fêtes polonaises des moissons, appelées dożynki, présentent à Dieu le travail des cultivateurs dans l'action de grâce. Lors d'une célébration diocésaine documentée, un évêque a béni des couronnes de moisson et des pains apportés par des communautés locales.
cards.meaning_en: The harvest gifts express gratitude for the fruits of the earth and solidarity with those who cultivate them.
cards.meaning_fr: Les offrandes des récoltes expriment la reconnaissance pour les fruits de la terre et la solidarité avec ceux qui les cultivent.
cards.suggested_observance_en: Where a parish holds a harvest thanksgiving, participate and assist with offerings as requested; do not attempt to perform the ministerial blessing yourself.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Lorsqu'une paroisse organise une action de grâce pour les moissons, y participer et contribuer selon les besoins ; ne pas improviser soi-même la bénédiction sacerdotale.

independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Polish episcopal account explicitly reports archbishop blessing harvest wreaths and bread during diocesan/provincial harvest celebration; source confirms a regional ministerial practice, not universal Roman calendar date.

cards.publication_caution: No global fixed dożynki date, mandatory harvest wreath or inferred universal 1962 blessing rite.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: Keeping the Nativity crib until Candlemas
cards.title_fr: Garder la crèche jusqu'à la Chandeleur
cards.occasion: 2 February, the Purification/Presentation in the 1962 calendar
cards.geographic_scope: Documented Catholic domestic practice, especially French custom
cards.existing_owner: Calendar / Customs Atlas; link to Candlemas existing DOM-011
cards.description_en: In some Catholic homes the Christmas crib remains in place until 2 February, the feast of the Presentation and Purification. This domestic custom extends contemplation of the Incarnation beyond the liturgical end of Christmas.
cards.description_fr: Dans certains foyers catholiques, la crèche de Noël reste installée jusqu'au 2 février, fête de la Présentation et de la Purification. Cette coutume familiale prolonge la contemplation de l'Incarnation au-delà de la fin liturgique du temps de Noël.
cards.meaning_en: The child's presentation in the Temple points toward Christ, the light recognised by Simeon.
cards.meaning_fr: La Présentation de l'Enfant au Temple oriente vers le Christ, lumière reconnue par Syméon.
cards.suggested_observance_en: Keep the crib until Candlemas if your family wishes, then gather briefly for a prayer before putting it away.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Garder la crèche jusqu'à la Chandeleur si on le souhaite, puis se réunir pour une courte prière avant de la ranger.

weiser_sources.source_title: Taking down Christmas crib on Candlemas

independent_witnesses.issuer: Diocese of Paris, La Chandeleur fête de la lumière (2014)
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Diocese explicitly distinguishes the end of liturgical Christmas from the domestic tradition of keeping a Nativity crib until Candlemas; not a universal removal requirement.

cards.publication_caution: Optional family tradition, not a liturgical order to change the Christmas season's dates or a competing Candlemas practice card.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: Caring for graves at All Souls
cards.title_fr: Prendre soin des tombes à la Toussaint et à la Commémoration des défunts
cards.occasion: Around 1–2 November and other family commemorations
cards.geographic_scope: Documented Catholic and Polish customs; local practice varies
cards.existing_owner: Enrich existing DEAD-001 / DEAD-003; never mint second Souls entry
cards.description_en: Families may visit cemeteries, clean or tend their relatives' graves, and place flowers or lights as signs of remembrance. Catholic teaching stresses that such visits accompany prayer for the departed, not a fearful obligation.
cards.description_fr: Des familles visitent les cimetières, entretiennent les tombes de leurs proches et y déposent des fleurs ou des lumières en signe de mémoire. L'enseignement catholique souligne que ces gestes accompagnent la prière pour les défunts et ne sont pas des obligations dictées par la peur.
cards.meaning_en: Charity toward departed souls is expressed most fully in prayer, hope and the Church's suffrages.
cards.meaning_fr: La charité envers les âmes des défunts s'exprime surtout dans la prière, l'espérance et les suffrages de l'Église.
cards.suggested_observance_en: If able, visit and tend a family grave, say a prayer for those buried there, or pray for the dead from home.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Si possible, entretenir et visiter une tombe familiale et y prier pour les défunts ; autrement, prier chez soi pour les âmes des fidèles défunts.

weiser_sources.source_title: Cleaning and decorating graves before November
All Souls lantern candles burning by tombs

independent_witnesses.issuer: Holy See, Directory on Popular Piety; Polish Bishops' Conference 31 Oct 2025
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Cemetery visits with tending graves, flowers and lamps acknowledged, while Polish bishops confirm local November family candle traditions; no mandatory grave visit or superstitious implications.

cards.publication_caution: Do not infer a mandatory cemetery visit, guaranteed indulgence, or deceased-name collection from these sources.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: St John Baptist's bonfire and community prayer
cards.title_fr: Le feu de la Saint-Jean-Baptiste et la prière communautaire
cards.occasion: Around 24 June, as announced by local community
cards.geographic_scope: Specific 2026 Catholic parish example in southwestern France
cards.existing_owner: Saints / Customs Atlas; local optional gathering
cards.description_en: Some Catholic parishes celebrate St John the Baptist with Mass, a shared meal, songs, prayers and an outdoor bonfire. A documented celebration in Oloron-Sainte-Marie illustrates this living local custom.
cards.description_fr: Certaines paroisses catholiques célèbrent saint Jean-Baptiste par une messe, un repas partagé, des chants, des prières et un feu de plein air. Une fête documentée à Oloron-Sainte-Marie illustre cette coutume locale encore vivante.
cards.meaning_en: The gathering places the Nativity of John the Baptist in a Christian community setting, recalling his mission to prepare Christ's way.
cards.meaning_fr: Le rassemblement replace la Nativité de saint Jean-Baptiste dans la vie de la communauté chrétienne et rappelle sa mission de préparer la venue du Christ.
cards.suggested_observance_en: Join only a properly organised local parish event; otherwise honour St John with prayer. Do not arrange a bonfire from app instructions.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Participer uniquement à une fête paroissiale organisée ; autrement, honorer saint Jean par la prière. L'application ne fournit pas d'instructions pour allumer un feu.

weiser_sources.source_title: St John Baptist eve hilltop bonfires
Community intercessory prayer beside St John bonfire

independent_witnesses.issuer: Diocese of Bayonne, Lescar and Oloron, Saint-Jean parish celebration 2026
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: A parish event near 24 June includes Mass, community bonfire, shared meal, songs and prayers; confirms one local celebration, not a church-mandated ceremony or all Breton sea-fire variants.

cards.publication_caution: Specific Breton fishermen and maritime fires remain unverified; no magic, guaranteed blessing or fire-making guidance.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: Tuesdays dedicated to St Anthony of Padua
cards.title_fr: Les mardis consacrés à saint Antoine de Padoue
cards.occasion: Nine or thirteen successive Tuesdays in some devotional traditions
cards.geographic_scope: Franciscan popular devotion, not a mandatory calendar cycle
cards.existing_owner: Existing Saints and Pray/Novena modules; no duplicate novena
cards.description_en: A Franciscan account documents a devotion to St Anthony on successive Tuesdays or Sundays, sometimes in cycles of nine or thirteen. Participants ask the saint's intercession through prayer; the form depends on the devotional community.
cards.description_fr: Un témoignage franciscain décrit la dévotion à saint Antoine pendant plusieurs mardis ou dimanches consécutifs, parfois durant neuf ou treize semaines. Les fidèles demandent son intercession par la prière, selon les usages du lieu.
cards.meaning_en: Steady prayer fosters perseverance and recalls the saint's love for Christ and the poor.
cards.meaning_fr: La prière régulière favorise la persévérance et rappelle l'amour du saint pour le Christ et les pauvres.
cards.suggested_observance_en: Use an already sourced St Anthony prayer or novena if desired, without expecting the devotion to produce a guaranteed favour.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Employer, si on le souhaite, une prière ou neuvaine déjà authentifiée en l'honneur du saint, sans en attendre une faveur garantie.

weiser_sources.source_title: Tuesday devotions and novenas for St Anthony

independent_witnesses.issuer: Franciscan Media, St Anthony of Padua traditions
independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Franciscan account reports nine or thirteen Tuesday or Sunday devotional cycles at churches and shrines; stories of promised miracles/old indulgences not treated as current guarantees.

cards.publication_caution: Historical 1898 indulgence, medieval stories and miracle guarantees are not presented as currently applicable.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

cards.title_en: A French patronal pardon at Sainte-Anne-d'Auray
cards.occasion: 25–26 July in the documented Breton shrine setting
cards.geographic_scope: Breton Catholic local pilgrimage celebration, not universal patronal feast form
cards.existing_owner: Enrich existing PATR-001 and Sainte Anne pilgrimage profile
cards.description_en: The Grand Pardon of Sainte-Anne-d'Auray illustrates a Breton patronal pilgrimage in which participants seek prayer, reconciliation and the saint's intercession. Its processions and Mass belong to a specific shrine and its local annual programme.
cards.description_fr: Le Grand Pardon de Sainte-Anne-d'Auray illustre un pèlerinage patronal breton où les fidèles recherchent la prière, la réconciliation et l'intercession de la sainte. Ses processions et sa messe appartiennent à un sanctuaire et à son programme local.
cards.meaning_en: A pardon joins pilgrimage, conversion and shared veneration of a heavenly patron.
cards.meaning_fr: Le pardon associe pèlerinage, conversion et vénération commune d'un patron céleste.
cards.suggested_observance_en: If visiting a participating shrine, consult its authentic programme; elsewhere, honour your parish's actual patron without presuming the same rites.
cards.suggested_observance_fr: Dans un sanctuaire qui organise un pardon, consulter son programme ; ailleurs, honorer le véritable patron de sa paroisse sans supposer que les mêmes cérémonies s'y tiennent.

weiser_sources.source_title: Parish and diocesan patron feast celebrations

independent_witnesses.claim_supported_and_limitations: Specific Saint Anne patronal observance with pilgrimage, Mass, local procession and reconciliation; contributes a local example to existing PATR-001, no generalized parish patron calendar.

cards.publication_caution: One shrine witness cannot establish every French fête patronale or a locally unverified 1962 proper.
cards.copyright: Original EN and FR prose, book only factual locator

partial_evidence_holds.reason: The source covers seasonal penitence and gratitude but does not substantiate a dedicated Ember prayer custom specifically for deceased souls.

Good Friday recollection and penitence are supported but the precise household custom of minimal food alongside silence is not independently documented; modern fasting laws need separate jurisdiction/age handling.
General almsgiving for the deceased supported, but specific beans/peas/lentils as a named regional food custom not verified.
Living Breton Grand Pardon and French devotion documented; does not demonstrate Weiser's specific medieval chronology or extent in France.
Blessed branches placed on graves are documented, but cemetery visitation specifically during the Palm Sunday liturgical procession is not verified.
Contemporary forty-hour exposition/adoration in Lent documented; historical pre-Lenten carnival timing not established by this source.
Community cemetery prayer and visits supported; specific priestly formula for blessing graves is not documented in this witness.
Flowers and procession route decorations are documented, but woven wreaths on banners and a separate priestly wreath blessing have not been independently established.
July 26 celebration documented; does not demonstrate baptismal name-day customs for Annes in all French households (already general NDAY-001).
Pyrenean Catholic bonfire documented, but no independent Breton fishing-boat or maritime rite evidence.
